collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HUMOR AND ABSURDITY (HUM-01 to HUM-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Slapstick, silly noises, puns, pranks with permission, ridiculous coincidences, a little funny magic and animals being absurd. Nobody is the butt of the joke: everyone keeps their dignity, and the comedy needs no victim.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A child asks the elders a riddle that has them arguing for an hour: ask for the answer, or let them keep guessing.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has asked the elders a riddle: "What is bigger than the sea, smaller than a seed, and lives in a basket?" The elders have been arguing about it for an hour. (subject) is sitting very still and very quietly, enjoying (subject.him/her)self enormously.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: At last the elders give up. "Well? What is it?" (subject) beams. "I don't know. I made it up." There's a stunned silence. Then one elder laughs, and then all of them. (elder), one of the elders, refuses to give up and insists the answer is "a dream," and argues it for weeks. (subject) tells (elder), "That's right," but only (elder.him/her).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The guesses go on. An egg? A thought? A sleeping lizard? The riddle spreads through the whole village, and for days people shout guesses at (subject) across the paths. (subject) just smiles. Nobody ever finds out that the riddle had no answer, or rather, that it now has about forty.
